costTraps.what: Private subnets reaching S3 or DynamoDB through a NAT gateway instead of a free Gateway VPC endpoint. Figure shown is 10 TB/month at the us-east-1 NAT processing rate of about $0.045/GB; several Regions charge materially more
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer filtered to NAT Gateway data processing, cross-referenced with VPC Flow Logs destinations or S3 Storage Lens request volume; then list route tables for the absence of a gateway endpoint prefix list
costTraps.fix: Create Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and associate them with every private route table. Verify nothing depended on the NAT path (egress inspection appliances, third-party S3 proxies) and scope the endpoint policy

costTraps.what: NAT gateways in dev, test and sandbox VPCs that process almost no data. About $32.85/month each in us-east-1, $40-$68 in higher-cost Regions, billed whether idle or not, with partial hours billed as full hours. Figure shown is five accounts x three AZs
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost and Usage Report grouped by resource for NatGateway-Hours, joined against NAT gateway BytesOutToDestination in CloudWatch
costTraps.fix: Delete the gateways and use VPC endpoints for the few services actually called; for IPv6 use an egress-only internet gateway, which has no hourly and no per-GB charge. Do not apply this to production or to the staging environment that gates production

costTraps.what: Every public IPv4 address is billed about $0.005/hour (about $3.65/month) since 1 February 2024, attached or not - including addresses on running instances, load balancers, NAT gateways and public RDS endpoints. Figure shown is a 300-address estate
costTraps.howToDetect: VPC Public IP Insights, plus the PublicIPv4:InUseAddress usage type in the Cost and Usage Report
costTraps.fix: Move instances behind NAT or a load balancer, release unneeded Elastic IPs, and adopt IPv6 with an egress-only internet gateway where possible

costTraps.what: Log groups created with no retention policy (the default is never expire) plus unbounded ingestion. Ingestion is the larger half at about $0.50/GB in us-east-1 against about $0.03/GB-month storage. Figure shown is 200 GB/month ingest plus two years of accumulated storage
costTraps.howToDetect: describe-log-groups filtered to retentionInDays null, sorted by storedBytes; Cost Explorer split between CloudWatch DataProcessing-Bytes and TimedStorage-ByteHrs
costTraps.fix: Set retention on every group and enforce it at creation; move high-volume low-query groups to the Infrequent Access log class (no Live Tail, metric filters or subscription filters); send VPC Flow Logs to S3 in Parquet instead of CloudWatch; trim debug logging left on after an incident

costTraps.what: EKS clusters whose Kubernetes version has passed end of standard support while the cluster upgrade policy is EXTENDED (the default), billed at $0.60 per cluster-hour instead of $0.10. Figure shown is five stale clusters
costTraps.howToDetect: describe-cluster for each cluster, checking version against the EKS release calendar's end-of-standard-support dates and reading upgradePolicy.supportType
costTraps.fix: Set supportType=STANDARD so AWS auto-upgrades at end of standard support and the extended rate never applies; where a vendor workload blocks an upgrade, budget for it and set an end date

costTraps.what: Unattached EBS volumes, snapshots whose source volume was deleted, load balancers with no targets, and interface endpoints nobody calls - all billing on provisioned time
costTraps.howToDetect: describe-volumes with state=available; describe-snapshots joined against existing volume ids; ELB RequestCount at zero over 7 days; endpoint ENI traffic at zero
costTraps.fix: Sweep and delete on a schedule, with a tag that exempts deliberate DR standbys and partner-allow-listed addresses. Move a last-copy snapshot to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier (90-day minimum) rather than deleting it

costTraps.what: Failed or abandoned multipart uploads leaving parts that bill as storage indefinitely and do NOT appear in ListObjects, so the bucket looks small while the bill grows
costTraps.howToDetect: S3 Storage Lens incomplete multipart upload bytes, or ListMultipartUploads per bucket
costTraps.fix: Add an AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule (commonly 7 days, longer than your longest legitimate upload) to every bucket that accepts multipart uploads

costTraps.what: A blanket lifecycle rule transitioning short-lived or small objects into Standard-IA or Glacier, paying minimum-duration charges (30/90/180 days), the 128 KB minimum billable object size, and per-object transition REQUEST fees that are highest for the Glacier classes
costTraps.howToDetect: S3 Storage Lens average object size and object count per prefix against the transition rules in the bucket lifecycle configuration; look for early-delete charges in the Cost and Usage Report
costTraps.fix: Remove transitions for objects below 128 KB or with lifetimes shorter than the class minimum; use Intelligent-Tiering where the pattern is unknown (no minimum duration, no retrieval fee, no monitoring fee below 128 KB); aggregate small objects before archiving

costTraps.what: A versioned bucket where an expiration rule was added but noncurrent versions and delete markers were not expired, so the deleted data keeps billing forever
costTraps.howToDetect: S3 Storage Lens noncurrent version bytes and delete marker counts, compared against current version bytes
costTraps.fix: Add NoncurrentVersionExpiration and ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker rules alongside the expiration rule; exclude anything under Object Lock or legal hold

costTraps.what: A chatty service pair, cache or service mesh spread evenly across AZs, charged about $0.01/GB at each end so about $0.02/GB in total. Figure shown is 100 TB/month of internal chatter in us-east-1
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost and Usage Report usage types containing DataTransfer-Regional-Bytes, attributed with VPC Flow Logs including the pkt-srcaddr and pkt-dstaddr fields
costTraps.fix: Topology-aware or zonal routing that prefers same-AZ targets while keeping capacity in every AZ. Never collapse to one AZ to save this, and never apply it to quorum systems. Check the carve-outs first - RDS Multi-AZ replication, Aurora cluster-volume traffic and ELB-to-target regional transfer are not charged

costTraps.what: SageMaker real-time endpoints and Lambda provisioned concurrency billing on provisioned time while serving little or no traffic. A single idle GPU-class endpoint can exceed the figure shown
costTraps.howToDetect: SageMaker Invocations at zero over 7 days; Lambda ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization below 0.2
costTraps.fix: Delete the endpoint or move to serverless or asynchronous inference; remove provisioned concurrency outside the launch window it was bought for

costTraps.what: Dev, test and staging instances and databases running all week. A weekday 8-hour schedule removes about 76% of the HOURS (40 of 168) but NOT 76% of the spend
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer filtered by environment tag with a usage-hours metric; compare against business hours
costTraps.fix: Attach an Instance Scheduler, but compute the real saving first: stopped EC2 still bills EBS and public IPv4, stopped RDS still bills storage and backups AND auto-restarts after 7 days, and an existing Savings Plan keeps billing unless production absorbs the freed commitment. Aurora Serverless v2 with min_capacity=0 achieves this without a scheduler

costTraps.what: A Savings Plan or Reserved Instance bought above the provable baseline, or bought per account rather than at the organization level. Commitments are non-cancellable and non-refundable for the whole term, so the unused portion is a pure loss
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer Savings Plans utilisation and coverage reports; look for utilisation below 100% and for accounts with their own commitments while the payer has spare
costTraps.fix: Size to the provable baseline, prefer Compute Savings Plans (which also cover Fargate and Lambda and survive a re-platform), and let consolidated billing share the commitment across the organization. Standard RIs can be resold on the Marketplace only with seller registration, a US bank account and 30 days remaining; Savings Plans cannot be sold at all

costTraps.what: Aurora standard configuration billing per I/O request on an I/O-heavy workload, where Aurora I/O-Optimized would have been cheaper
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost and Usage Report usage types containing Aurora:StorageIOUsage as a share of total Aurora spend
costTraps.fix: Switch the cluster to I/O-Optimized when I/O is a large share of Aurora spend; the switch is a cluster configuration change, so model both before moving

costTraps.what: CloudWatch custom metrics at about $0.30 per metric per month with high-cardinality dimensions, PutMetricData API charges, X-Ray traces, Contributor Insights, and AWS Config configuration items in churn-heavy accounts
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer for CloudWatch split by usage type (MetricMonitorUsage, Requests) and for Config ConfigurationItemRecorded; count distinct metric names and dimension combinations
costTraps.fix: Emit metrics from logs with the Embedded Metric Format instead of PutMetricData per call, cap metric cardinality explicitly, and scope the Config recorder by resource type or use periodic recording - do NOT switch Config off, because most Security Hub CSPM controls then silently stop evaluating

costTraps.what: CloudTrail data events (S3 object-level, Lambda invoke) enabled bucket-wide on a high-volume bucket, and a member-account trail duplicating an organization trail
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer for CloudTrail usage types; describe-trails per account looking for local trails alongside the org trail
costTraps.fix: Scope data events to sensitive prefixes rather than everywhere, and remove duplicate local trails - management events are free for the first trail only, so a second trail duplicates the cost without adding evidence

costTraps.what: AWS Budgets stamped into every account at scale. Anomaly detection is free; Budgets is free only for the FIRST TWO per account and then costs about $0.02 per budget per day (about $0.60/month each), with Budget actions charged separately. Figure shown is six budgets across 200 accounts
costTraps.howToDetect: Cost Explorer for the AWS Budgets usage type; count budgets per account across the organization
costTraps.fix: Centralise budgets in the management account with per-linked-account scope rather than duplicating objects everywhere - the requirement is coverage, not one object per account
